📖 COURSE DESCRIPTION

This advanced digital media arts course transitions from individual asset creation to orchestrating complex multimedia systems. Students master interoperable pipelines, bridging disparate software environments including Blender, iPad 3D modeling, Minecraft Education Edition, TouchDesigner, and Roblox Studio to create unified, interactive performance art and installations. The course emphasizes system integration, data-driven visual logic, and transmedia storytelling.

CTE & Pipeline Focus: Students operate as technical directors, utilizing official API manuals and documentation to bridge pipelines. Key milestones include a Procedural Environment (Blender and UE5), iPad to 3D Print Physicality, Spatial UI Prototyping (Minecraft and TouchDesigner), and a Networked Multi-User Experience (Roblox and TouchDesigner).

🎯 COURSE GOALS & STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES (SLO)

(Official language from the DMA 90 Course Outline of Record [COR])

Student Learning Outcomes (SLOs)

Upon completion of the course, the student should be able to:

  • Examine principles, procedures, and systems for the creation of computer generated art.
  • Develop a personal system of critical evaluation for digital imagery and interrelationships within the various fields of computer graphics.
  • Design, create, and produce a resolved computer art portfolio.

Course Objectives

  • Apply Mobile to Physical Workflows: Utilize iPad based modeling tools to create precision assets, transition through 3D printing, and execute high fidelity projection mapping calibration via TouchDesigner.
  • Master Data Driven Visuals: Apply real time visual programming (TouchDesigner and GLSL) to translate geometric data from external environments like Minecraft and Roblox into interactive spatial projections.
  • Implement Procedural Animation and Networking: Master procedural geometry and networked multi user architecture (Roblox Studio) to build immersive real time interactive experiences.
  • Analyze Technical Constraints: Evaluate the performance and scalability of cross platform software integration, troubleshooting latency and interoperability hurdles in a professional pipeline.

🖥️ COURSE FORMAT & INSTRUCTIONAL METHODS

This course is partially online, with in-person meetings in LAC-L175.

  • Means of Instruction: A mix of in-person lecture, laboratory studio work, and online instructional delivery. Methods include live demonstrations, developer documentation tutorials, quickstart guides, structured critique, immersive VR and XR testing, projection mapping calibration, project based learning, individual and team assignments, and online web publishing.
  • Online Component: Students will access supplementary technical documentation, pre-recorded tutorials, and project submissions through the Canvas learning management system. Collaborative project reviews and troubleshooting sessions may also be conducted via Zoom.
  • Outside Assignment Hours: In compliance with California Title 5 guidelines, two hours of outside assignment work (72 out of class hours total across the term spent reading documentation, working on projects, researching, and publishing deliverables) are required for every one hour of lecture.
  • Submissions: All assignments are submitted digitally through Canvas, with live web portfolio deliverables and public portfolio showcases hosted on ArtStation and Sketchfab.

🎨 PORTFOLIO EMPHASIS

By the end of the semester, every student will complete and document a professional portfolio of advanced multimedia work, including:

  1. Procedural 3D Asset & Audio Project: Procedural assets developed in Blender with integrated audio and real-time elements.
  2. Interactive Projection Installation: Interactive spatial experience incorporating TouchDesigner, projection mapping, and real-time visual programming.
  3. Transmedia Narrative Piece: Multi-platform interactive experience combining digital media, narrative structure, and interactive systems.
  4. Advanced Demo Reel: Professionally edited reel featuring procedural modeling, character animation, PBR materials, real-time graphics, projection mapping, and interactive spatial design.
  5. ArtStation Portfolio: Curated presentation of completed projects with documentation, technical process, images, video, and final deliverables.

Examination & Evaluation Note

This course does not use traditional examinations. Learning is continuously evaluated through hands-on studio work, research and technical writing, interactive VR/XR and web deliverables, portfolio submissions, and active discussion participation.

  • To support different learning styles, experience levels, and creative interests, students may complete any Professor Ocean tutorial for UDL credit. Tutorials include game design, Blender, Maya, Mixamo, environmental VFX, animation, and related production workflows.
  • Students must complete the demonstrated work and submit the required evidence in Canvas to receive credit.

📌 CLASS POLICIES & COMPLIANCE

Attendance Policy

Attendance is the responsibility of the student. Students who do not attend the first class session may be dropped from the class at the discretion of the instructor. In the event of excessive absences, the instructor may drop a student from the course or may lower a student's grade. A course grade will never be based solely on attendance.

TBA Compliance

This course does not include TBA (To Be Arranged) hours. Both DMA 90-04 Lecture and DMA 90-04A Lab meet at fixed, scheduled times on Wednesdays in LAC-L175 for the full term, with no unscheduled or arranged-hours component.

Rules of Conduct

Students are expected to maintain a professional, respectful, and collaborative learning environment. Disruptive behavior, offensive language, or conduct that interferes with instruction, laboratory activities, or critiques is prohibited and may result in removal from class sessions and further disciplinary action in accordance with Long Beach City College policy.
